Dialogue writing is terrible. Handsome Jack from BL2 walked the tightrope between "annoying" and "villain you wanted to see dead" purely on the strength of his writing. 
Whoever they wrangled to write the antagonists' dialogue in BL3 doesn't even bother to toe that line - There are no redeeming qualities between the two of them and I would appreciate a mod that just removes all of their dialogue.
Bugs that have remained unaddressed since the launch of the game [x] number of years ago - Be ready to lose who your co-op partner is in the mess since the over-head player markers disappear within minutes of entering a zone.

I don't recommend this title for fans of the series, even at a price of less than $10 on sale. In fact, pretend the franchise died with the Pre-Sequel.

Look, it has better gameplay than BL2, but the story just.. Doesn't grab me. It was always going to be hard to follow up Handsome Jack, and the Calypso twins def struggle in that regard, but that isn't even the worst of it. None of the characters from the older games feel right. Lilith makes lots of dumb decisions, Tannis has become much more sociable & goofy, Rhys and Vaughn are BUTCHERED, and don't even get me started on Maya. The game suffers from the bandits being the main antagonists, The game suffers from each planet being essentially a show up, solve the issues of some local leader, then get to access their vault right after. The vaults on pandora were hard to open, but Eden-6? Promethea? No sweat at all. 

I won't get into the horribly overtuned drop rates, or the crimson raiders' change in leadership, or the excessive number of "quirky" character moments. But out of BL1, BL2, Presequel and this, it's definitely the weakest entry & the one with the least soul.

Anything past Borderlands 2 never happened and this game as well as Borderlands 4 were just hallucinations.

Sarcasm aside, this game is [i]okay[/i], but the story itself could've been better and the main villains are very generic and not really villains at all. The game is carried by its gameplay, and even that has its fair share with flaws, as with Borderlands 2.

citations.review_text:
Logged around 200+ hours on PS4.

​Great gunplay and a huge step up from Borderlands 2. 

The main story can be quite annoying, but the DLCs are actually good. 

Performance is decent overall.

​10/10 — Gearbox is going strong.

Borderlands 3 is yet another solid entry in the franchise. It's exactly what you'd expect from a Borderlands game, but reworked and improved in all the right ways.

[b]First, I'll start with the POSITIVES:[/b]
+ The looter-shooter gameplay is absolute crack. The loop goes: find an overpowered gun → use it until it becomes average → replace it with an even better gun → repeat. It's an endless cycle of chasing the next OP weapon, and the gameplay loop is honestly near perfect.
+ The gameplay itself is top-tier. Between the skill trees, player progression, huge variety of enemies, and endless weapons, the game stayed fresh almost all the way to the end.
+ No complaints about performance. I didn't experience any crashes, bugs, or noticeable glitches. It was a super smooth experience.
+ There's a solid 30 hours of content just in the main game, and probably closer to 40 if you take your time and complete the side stuff
+ It's a great "turn your brain off" shooter. You can relax and just enjoy blasting through enemies for most of the game. (This could be a negative for some people, but it's exactly what I was looking for.)

[b]Here are some NEGATIVES that come to mind:[/b]
- The story is pretty dumb. I'm still not sure how I feel about the main villains being an influencer/streamer duo.
- Some of the map design is a chore. It feels like certain areas were made unnecessarily huge just to pad the game's length.
- Sanctuary is awful to navigate. Why does it have three floors with almost no cohesive flow between them?
- The Borderlands humor and overall atmosphere didn't feel as fresh this time around. I miss when most of the characters were just completely insane. It felt more tame.

Overall, I'd give Borderlands 3 a 3.5/5. The gameplay loop is what will always keep me coming back to this series. I got exactly what I wanted from Borderlands, and even a little more.

My Rating: ⭐⭐⭐✨✨ 3.5 / 5

Super corny, DLC is hit or miss, but it feels [b]really[/b] good to play. It will probably be torture playing it solo. If you can somehow manage to get a friend to buy the ultimate edition alongside you, even the terrible parts can shine a little. Wait for a 90% sale, they happen pretty often now.

Oh, and the performance is insane. I'm running it maxed out and even with a gazillion effects on my screen the 1% lows don't move. No idea how the same devs managed to make BL4.
Runs smooth and looks great!

This is easily the weakest game in the Borderlands franchise. Normally I'd say the story doesn't really matter in a looter shooter, but in this case it's so painfully bad that it actually gets in the way of enjoying the game. I skipped every cutscene I could, and whenever I couldn't, it felt like the game was holding me hostage.

As if that wasn't enough, the characters never seem to shut up. Even after the cutscenes are over, they're constantly talking to you over the radio, and most of the dialogue ranges from forgettable to downright irritating. By the end of the campaign, I was more excited to mute the voices than to hear the next mission.

Thankfully, the gameplay carries the entire experience. The gunplay is excellent, the loot system is as addictive as ever, and blowing up bandits with ridiculous weapons never gets old. That's what Borderlands has always been about, and it's the only reason I kept playing.

If you've had a long day at work or school and just want to switch your brain off, throw on some music, and turn thousands of psychos into loot piñatas, this game still delivers. It took me around 30 hours to finish the campaign, and despite everything I genuinely had fun because the core gameplay is that good.

For under €10, it's absolutely worth picking up. Just do yourself a favor tho and skip every cutscene you can, let the loot do the talking, and pretend the story never happened.

I recommend this one mainly for the gameplay, the guns and looting system feel really fun to play and ultimately, that's really what you want out of a game.

As many have said the story, dialogs, and characters are terrible, unfunny, and unlikeable. Delivering coffee to a purple haired, nose ring Karen, and having to deal with cringe furries is really annoying. I guarantee the writers probably look like the characters they designed.

I recommend you don't play this game for the plot, just skip the cut scenes and turn the dialog audio to 0. Also, don't pay full price for this either.

I've played the main story and the side quests of the main story to completion, and I'm sad to say the story is still too loud and awful for me to ignore.

Gameplay wise, this game is very strong, and surpasses the groundwork laid by Borderlands 2. It's fun as ♥♥♥♥.

But the writing, story, and everything outside of the gameplay is overbearingly millennial-coded. Like, Rick and Morty core humor that will have you rolling your eyes and throwing up a little every time almost any character says something that isn't exposition.

It's a shame too, because there's a lot of potential with a story that implicates the cast of Borderlands 1 and 2, but none of those interesting dimensions you'd expect are explored or exploited. They get turned into tools for Borderlands 3's narrative to exist, oftentimes mischaracterizing or recharacterizing beloved characters so Borderlands 3's events can happen. It's disappointing, and overshadows much of the good Borderlands 3 gets right.

citations.review_text:
A good game that needs to be rescued from Gearbox at this point - they've made it almost impossible to enjoy.

+ graphics and sound design are fantastic
+ gun design is a major improvement over the monstrously ugly mess that was BL2's guns
+ polished and very enjoyable gunplay; traversal is also fairly fast, smooth and flows very well

- Legendary loot drops are so ridiculously common it kills all excitement for drops
- maps are unironically too big and quests are time-wasting traversals (go to A, wait for NPC to yap for literal minutes, go to B; take item 2 meters away, give to NPC)
- dozens of Ubisoft-esque "wait for this NPC to finish yapping"/ "follow this slow NPC" segments, genuine waste of time
- boss fights generally suck; almost all bosses have phases that slow the pace to a crawl and makes min-maxing builds worthless, after a point any bonus dmg you do is irrelevant since you hit the boss' phase and wait around for its invincibility to end
- everyone in BL is gay - the amount of LGBTQ prevalence is kinda crazy, most (yes, actually) of the NPCs in game who's sexuality is mentioned are gay/lesbian. There is an entire DLC dedicated to marrying two gay men. Heterosexuality is merely implied to exist in this universe. Very strange and blatantly propagandistic
- the humor keeps becoming more and more unbearable. Zoomers will find this hard to believe but BL1's humor was fairly understated, the most "wacky" NPCs were Claptrap and Tannis, and even they have been flanderized beyond recognition. The reddit-fication of the franchise began with BL2 and and reached an unbearable degree

The main story is abysmally bad, but it is undoubtably the best gameplay and gunplay in the series. It feels so good to run around and shoot stuff. All the characters are unique and fun to play. While legendaries are far more plentiful than any other game in the series, there are so many cool and fun ones with amazing synergies. The soundtrack is amazing, Jesper Kyd and Raison Varner crushed it. The Maliwan Takedown alone is better than anything BL4 can put out and that's only ONE of the FREE dlcs they added. The Halloween event is amazing, the Cartel event is amazing. This game is so good it makes me sad to see how BL4 ended up.

I don't think anyone needs a commentary on how abysmal the campaign and many side quest story lines are. This is known information at this point.
Aside from this, bosses are designed well, have well thought out mechanics that make them enjoyable to fight.
Mayhem mode is a mixed bag, it can add sufficient complexity for those looking for a somewhat chaotic experience, though I often find myself playing with it disabled or on mayhem 11 to ignore the modifiers. Locking some drops behind mayhem mode serves to push players into it, which is probably fine, but I can see it rubbing some the wrong way. Build diversity also takes a nose dive after some mayhem levels as certain weapons simply scale better, how big a deal this is will depend on the person in particular. You can technically make anything work, it will just take years to kill anything.
The legendary designs for the most part are fantastic, featuring some returning items and plenty of new ones. I like a lot of them.
Level design is not super condensed, I feel it could have used a smaller map in several locations, but for the most part it isn't egregious and can be traversed without too much effort, though it does feel like many areas call for a car. (or a good snowdrift/speed zane build)
The fps elements are vastly improved compared to BL2, it is fun to simply move around in the environments and shot the guns give to you, regardless of whether or not they are legendary. Sliding and mantling are not revolutionary, but they feel satisfying to use.
The characters are all unique in their own ways and have varied playstyles, I have completed entire playthroughs of each except flak. And can safely say that they are all very fun in their own ways, and have several viable ways to build their skill trees.

[h2]3/5[/h2]

I’m a fan of the Borderlands franchise, but this was a really hard playthrough, both for my friends and me. And it’s mainly because of the story, because in every other way, the game seems to have upgraded. Sadly, I neither have the time nor the interest to play the DLCs, so I will not be including them in my review.

I started the game in co-op with my friends, but they gave up midway through the main story because they felt incredibly overwhelmed with completely unnecessary dialogue, to the point where you either forget or simply lose track of what the point of your mission even is. I do know that the Borderlands lore is quite huge, but even by Borderlands standards, this is some bad storywriting. The yapping is f*cking excessive, especially considering the amount of characters involved at the same time. However, I can say that the last 2-3 hours felt quite entertaining, mainly because the unnecessary characters are stripped away and you can finally focus on the plot. Most of the characters are already familiar, and I think the concept of the villains would work well with the Calypso twins, if they weren’t so incredibly cringy. [spoiler]And the fact that they USED the death of Maya, one of the franchise’s icons, completely unnecessary, purely to make players feel something toward the villains, tells you a lot about how lame the storytelling is.[/spoiler]
This also completely tanks the replay value, in my personal opinion, because all of those dialogues are completely unskippable, and some of them are up to 4 minutes long. Overall, the story is simply paced terribly and it’s just completely forgettable.

Other than all that the game is amazing. The gunplay is fast and heavy. All four vault hunters are a joy to play. Build crafting is really fun in this game maybe even better than in Bl2. The game runs well the graphics are above par. Picking this up on sale is a no brainer. Its a great modern version of Bl2 

8/10
For the absolute smoothest, most fluid, and modern FPS mechanics - pick this game. The only weak point is the story which you can ignore and skip.

The main story is abysmally bad, but it is undoubtably the best gameplay and gunplay in the series. It feels so good to run around and shoot stuff. All the characters are unique and fun to play. While legendaries are far more plentiful than any other game in the series, there are so many cool and fun ones with amazing synergies. The soundtrack is amazing, Jesper Kyd and Raison Varner crushed it. The Maliwan Takedown alone is better than anything BL4 can put out and that's only ONE of the FREE dlcs they added. The Halloween event is amazing, the Cartel event is amazing. This game is so good it makes me sad to see how BL4 ended up.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that legendary loot drops are extremely common.

citations.review_text:
A good game that needs to be rescued from Gearbox at this point - they've made it almost impossible to enjoy.

+ graphics and sound design are fantastic
+ gun design is a major improvement over the monstrously ugly mess that was BL2's guns
+ polished and very enjoyable gunplay; traversal is also fairly fast, smooth and flows very well

- Legendary loot drops are so ridiculously common it kills all excitement for drops
- maps are unironically too big and quests are time-wasting traversals (go to A, wait for NPC to yap for literal minutes, go to B; take item 2 meters away, give to NPC)
- dozens of Ubisoft-esque "wait for this NPC to finish yapping"/ "follow this slow NPC" segments, genuine waste of time
- boss fights generally suck; almost all bosses have phases that slow the pace to a crawl and makes min-maxing builds worthless, after a point any bonus dmg you do is irrelevant since you hit the boss' phase and wait around for its invincibility to end
- everyone in BL is gay - the amount of LGBTQ prevalence is kinda crazy, most (yes, actually) of the NPCs in game who's sexuality is mentioned are gay/lesbian. There is an entire DLC dedicated to marrying two gay men. Heterosexuality is merely implied to exist in this universe. Very strange and blatantly propagandistic
- the humor keeps becoming more and more unbearable. Zoomers will find this hard to believe but BL1's humor was fairly understated, the most "wacky" NPCs were Claptrap and Tannis, and even they have been flanderized beyond recognition. The reddit-fication of the franchise began with BL2 and and reached an unbearable degree

The main story is abysmally bad, but it is undoubtably the best gameplay and gunplay in the series. It feels so good to run around and shoot stuff. All the characters are unique and fun to play. While legendaries are far more plentiful than any other game in the series, there are so many cool and fun ones with amazing synergies. The soundtrack is amazing, Jesper Kyd and Raison Varner crushed it. The Maliwan Takedown alone is better than anything BL4 can put out and that's only ONE of the FREE dlcs they added. The Halloween event is amazing, the Cartel event is amazing. This game is so good it makes me sad to see how BL4 ended up.
